cases.statement: One carrier: Patient 5 of a five-child Chinese series (Henan Children's Hospital).

people.label: Patient 5
people.key_phenotypes: age 1y6m at genetic diagnosis; recurrent fever; oral ulcers; ulcers in ileocecum and ascending, transverse and descending colon; motor and cognitive development delay

| Oral ulcers | YES | NO | YES | NO | YES |

Patient 5 presented with ulcers in the ileocecum, ascending colon, transverse colon, and descending colon.

phenotype_specificity.statement: Recurrent fever, oral ulcers and extensive colonic ulcers. Motor and cognitive developmental delay is also recorded, and the paper does not explain it. No other candidate variants are reported for Patient 5; the series used WES with Sanger confirmation.

quotes.quote: | Motor and cognitive development delay | YES | NO | NO | NO | YES |
Genetic testing data from whole-exome sequencing (WES), along with demographic, clinical, and laboratory data, were collected for each child.

segregation.statement: not reported. No family history in any patient.

quotes.quote: None of the patients reported a family history of genetic disorders or any special allergies.

de_novo.statement: Stated de novo for all patients after testing of origin. The paper does not say which relatives were tested, and parentage confirmation is not reported.

quotes.quote: All patients were de novo (they have all been tested to confirm their origin).
Further analysis indicated that the variants in all patients were de novo.

functional.statement: not reported. The authors note no functional validation.

quotes.quote: Secondly, the newly identified variants were classified solely based on the ACMG criteria without functional validation

variant_type_and_mechanism.statement: Four-nucleotide deletion predicted to cause a frameshift (p.(Lys635IlefsTer61)) in the zinc-finger region per the authors. The paper attributes the disease to loss of A20 function.

quotes.quote: In our study, two TNFAIP3 variants affected the ZnF domain (patients 2, 5)
In HA20 patients, variants in TNFAIP3 typically result in loss-of-function of the A20 protein

authors_classification.statement: ACMG-based classification with criteria, as stated by the authors.

quotes.quote: c.1903_1906del AAAC: p. K635fs* 61 (PVS1_Very strong + PS2_Moderate + PM2_Supporting) were classified as pathogenic per ACMG criteria.

concerns: 41890736 has several internal inconsistencies about which patient has which finding (MMACHC variants given to patient 2 or 3; Table 3 mislabels the c.133C>T case). Treat patient-level details with care.
The paper's protein notation 'p. K635fs* 61' leaves out the new residue. The batch predicts p.(Lys635IlefsTer61).
Motor and cognitive developmental delay is not typical of the disease as the paper describes it, and is not explained. Follow-up was only 1 month.
This series overlaps in patients with 40859316 (at least one child with identical lab values). That paper does not report this variant, so the overlap does not affect this candidate.
Transcript stated is NM_006290.5, not the batch's NM_001270508.2.
notes_for_panel: Single de novo case. No functional or segregation data.
